svg.title: The FieldLink feed sync as a durable orchestration, with its monitoring
svg.desc: The function app func-cedar-fieldlink-dev. On the left, how a run starts: the timer function FeedSweep at 02:00, 03:00 and 04:00 Amman time lists the blob folder inbox, and the HTTP function StartSync accepts POST api/sync-runs/name and answers 202 with a status URL. Both compute the hash of the file content and use it as the orchestration instance ID, feed-hash, so that one content has one run: a running instance is not started again and completed content is moved to the archive as a duplicate. In the middle, the orchestrator FeedSync: it calls the activity PrepareFeed, which reads and validates the file and returns counts and the number of chunks; then it loops: the activity ApplyChunk applies chunk i to Dataverse as the application user FieldLink Sync Functions through the bulk writer of lesson 78; when the result says throttled, the orchestrator waits with a durable timer for the time Dataverse asked, bounded between 30 seconds and 15 minutes, and applies the same chunk again, at most six waits; when all chunks are done it calls FinishFeed, which writes a report blob, moves the file to archive, or to quarantine when the file was rejected, and logs the line cedar.fieldlinkSync. On the right, the stores: the blob container fieldlink-feeds with inbox, archive, quarantine and reports, the task hub with history and instances, and Dataverse. At the bottom, monitoring: the status endpoint shows runtime status and custom status with chunks done; Application Insights receives the log lines cedar.fieldlinkChunk, cedar.fieldlinkThrottled and cedar.fieldlinkSync; the timer function SyncWatch at 05:30 asks the task hub and the inbox whether the night finished and logs cedar.fieldlinkSyncWatch with findings SYNC-01 to SYNC-04; one alert rule fires on anything other than a clean completion.

Monitoring: three ways to ask "what happened?"
